Name: Mesón de Cándido
Tips: Spain's most famous cochinillo restaurant since 1884 — 5 generations of the Cándido family. Directly beneath the Aqueduct arch. Plate-smashing ceremony performed straight-faced. Every Spanish president 3 monarchs Hemingway Bobby Fischer Dalai Lama have eaten here. BOOK NOW for Fri Sep 4 13:30 — summer Fridays fill. Open daily lunch 13:00–16:30 dinner 20:00–23:00. +34 921 425 911. candido@mesondecandido.es

Name: Restaurante José María
Tips: Critics' choice for best cochinillo in Segovia — more refined less theatrical. Founded 1982 by José María Ruíz. Restored building one block from Plaza Mayor. Deepest wine list in Segovia (own-label Ribera del Duero). Open every day of the year kitchen from 12:30. Online booking on website; under 48h phone +34 921 461 111 or reservas@restaurantejosemaria.com.

Name: Casa Duque
Tips: Third of the classic cochinillo trio (since 1895). Rustic stone-vaulted dining rooms on multiple levels. Same plate-smashing tradition as Cándido — quieter slightly cheaper. 5th-generation Duque family still runs it. Good backup if first two booked. Also excellent cordero asado. +34 921 462 487.

Name: El Fogón Sefardí
Address: C/ de la Judería Vieja 17 40001 Segovia
Tips: A completely different angle on Segovia food — Sephardic-influenced cuisine in a restored medieval building in the Jewish Quarter. No cochinillo on the menu (Jewish dietary laws). Lamb tagine eggplant in honey gallina trufada trenza segoviana. Atmospheric candle-lit small. +34 921 466 250.

Name: La Concepción
Tips: Lighter modern café-restaurant on the Plaza Mayor. Good if family wants casual lunch instead of 2-hour cochinillo experience — tapas salads ponche segoviano. Walk-in fine.

Name: Mesón Mayor
Tips: Plaza Mayor mid-range less famous than the cochinillo trio but does the same wood-fired roasts at lower prices. Decent backup.

Name: La Cocina de Segovia
Address: Plaza Mayor 12 40001 Segovia (inside Hotel Infanta Isabel)
Tips: Quietly excellent — less famous so less booked. Castilian classics done well. View over Plaza Mayor from some tables. +34 921 461 300.

Name: Confitería El Alcázar
Tips: THE inventor of the ponche segoviano — Ponche Segoviano® is their registered trademark since 1926. On the Plaza Mayor (old notes said C/ Marqués del Arco — wrong; it's Plaza Mayor 13). Also florones mantecadas yemas. Open daily ~10:00–19:00 — go before 19:00 or use Limón y Menta. +34 921 462 118.

Name: Pastelería Limón y Menta
Tips: The locals' other favourite for ponche segoviano — 30 seconds off the Plaza Mayor. Excellent café con leche; a few outdoor tables face the square. Open Fri to 20:30 — the reliable evening ponche stop. +34 921 462 141.

Name: Cafetería Limón y Menta (breakfast)
Tips: Breakfast at the edge of the Plaza Mayor — café con leche + tostada con tomate the classic Spanish breakfast. Outdoor seats. Only if you arrive hungry — the Aqueduct comes first.

Name: Café Jeyma
Tips: Local working-class café near the Aqueduct — €3 desayuno completo (coffee + tostada + juice).

Name: Helados Acueducto
Tips: Genuine Italian gelato 2-min walk from the Aqueduct — perfect post-cochinillo cool-down. Stracciatella limón pistachio.

Name: El Rincon de Vero
Tips: LOCALS TIER Menu del dia with four starters four mains dessert and drink Sopa castellana judiones chocolate cheese cake Weekend menu also available Small room

Name: Restaurante California
Tips: Home cooking judiones cod salad asparagus piquillos homemade desserts and cochinillo Small so reserve One of the best cheap but good options in town

Name: La Panera
Tips: Very cheap daily menu plus a traditional menu with roast cochinillo and judiones Good when half the table wants the roast and half wants a 12 EUR lunch

Name: De Bote en Bote
Tips: Central tapas and raciones modern list with vegetarian options The no ceremony alternative to a two hour roast lunch
